question: Functions of plasmin are all except-
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Plasmin" -> "Activation of collagenase" -> "Possible role in tissue remodeling" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Plasmin" -> "Destruction of VWF" -> "Possible degradation of von Willebrand factor" -> 70%
analysis: Plasmin is an important enzyme in the fibrinolytic system, primarily responsible for breaking down fibrin clots, a process known as fibrinolysis. It also plays a role in activating collagenase, which is involved in the breakdown of collagen. Plasmin can degrade von Willebrand factor (VWF) to some extent. However, stabilization of fibrin is not a function of plasmin; rather, it is the role of factor XIII, which cross-links fibrin to stabilize the clot.
